# ExpressoTS

> TypeScript-first Node.js framework built on Express 5: dependency injection,
> lifecycle hooks, providers, guards, interceptors, events, and a testing
> toolkit. Ships as @expressots/core, @expressots/adapter-express and the
> @expressots/cli scaffolder. Requires Node >= 20.19 (Bun is supported).

This file indexes the documentation for the current major (4.x).
The full text of every page is at https://doc.expresso-ts.com/llms-full.txt.

## Write code for v4, not v3

The entry point is `bootstrap`:

```ts
import { bootstrap } from "@expressots/core";
import { App } from "./app"; // class App extends AppExpress

void bootstrap(App);
```

Names removed in v4 that models trained on v3 still produce:

- `AppFactory` / `AppFactory.create()` -> use `await bootstrap(App)`. Since 4.3.0
  importing it compiles to an error that names the replacement.
- `InMemoryDataProvider` / `InMemoryDataTable` -> `InMemoryDBProvider`
- `LazyServiceIdentifer` (typo alias) -> `LazyServiceIdentifier`
- `AppContainer#viewContainerBindings` -> `introspect()` or `getFormattedBindingsView()`
- `.env` is no longer loaded implicitly -> call `loadEnvSync()` before `bootstrap`,
  or pass `envFileConfig` to `bootstrap`.

Every scaffolded project carries an AGENTS.md with these rules, and
`expressots llms` prints the guidance matching the installed package version.

## CORE

- [First steps](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/core/first-steps): Scaffold and run an ExpressoTS v4 project in five minutes.
- [Bootstrap](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/core/bootstrap): Zero-configuration application startup with comprehensive deployment options.
- [App](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/core/app-provider): The App class is the core of an ExpressoTS application.
- [Container](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/core/app-container): The AppContainer manages dependency injection configuration.
- [Modules](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/core/module): Modules are collections of controllers.
- [Controllers](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/core/controller): Controllers the mediator between the client and server.
- [Use cases](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/core/usecase): Use cases represents the business logic of the application.
- [Providers](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/core/providers): Modular services with DI scopes, optional capabilities, and publishable packages.
- [Lifecycle Hooks](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/core/lifecycle): Manage application and provider lifecycle with hooks.
- [Injection](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/core/di): Dependency Injection in ExpressoTS.
- [Entities](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/core/entities): Entities are objects that represent data.

## FEATURES

- [Interceptors](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/features/interceptors): Aspect-oriented programming with interceptors for cross-cutting concerns like logging, caching, transformation, and timing.
- [Event System](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/features/events): Type-safe, auto-discovered event system for decoupled architecture.
- [Guards & Authorization](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/features/guards): Comprehensive guard system for authentication and authorization.
- [Authorization Setup](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/features/authorization): Wire up the v4 authorization subsystem with one call - permission hierarchy, caching, preloading, and your AuthProvider.
- [Lazy Loading](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/features/lazy-loading): Zero-config lazy loading with auto-detection, warmup strategies, and performance optimization.
- [Testing Module](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/features/testing): Comprehensive testing utilities for unit, integration, and E2E testing.
- [Logging System](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/features/logging): Production-ready logging with 11 comprehensive phases including structured logging, transports, redaction, monitoring, and query capabilities.
- [Enhanced Configuration](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/features/configuration): Type-safe configuration management with validation and environment switching.
- [Middleware](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/features/middleware): Middleware are interceptors.
- [Decorators](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/features/decorators): Reference for every decorator shipped by ExpressoTS v4: DI, controllers, methods, parameters, validation, content negotiation, AOP, security, events, and lifecycle.
- [Status code](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/features/status-code): Use the StatusCode enum to set HTTP status codes consistently across controllers, use cases, and errors.
- [Error handling](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/features/error-handling): Error handling in ExpressoTS v4: typed app errors, RFC 7807 problem details, exception filters, and the Report helper.
- [Render engine](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/features/render): How to render views in ExpressoTS.
- [ExpressoTS config](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/features/expressots-config): ExpressoTS configuration file.
- [DTO validator](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/features/dto-validator): Use the v4 validation system with class-validator, Zod, or Yup for DTO payload validation.
- [Env validator](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/features/envvalidator): Validate environment variables in v4 with defineConfig + Env.* and loadEnvSync.
- [DB in memory](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/features/in-memory-db): A Prisma-like in-memory database for development, testing, and prototyping.
- [Content Negotiation](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/features/content-negotiation): RFC 7231-compliant content negotiation in ExpressoTS v4. Accept / Consumes / Produces decorators, built-in JSON / XML / CSV / YAML / plain-text formatters, and streaming responses.
- [Validation](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/features/validation): ExpressoTS v4 Smart Validation: Zod, Yup, class-validator, and custom adapters via a single registry and parameter decorators.
- [Exception Filters](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/features/exception-filters): Customize how ExpressoTS turns errors into HTTP responses with @Catch, @UseFilters, and BaseExceptionFilter.
- [Route Patterns](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/features/route-patterns): Type-safe regex constraints on route parameters using Patterns and pattern(): Express 5 / path-to-regexp v8 compatible.
- [API Versioning](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/features/api-versioning): Run multiple API versions side by side using @Version, with controller-level or method-level overrides.
- [Health & Monitoring](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/features/health-monitoring): Built-in middleware health endpoint, IHealthCheck providers, and the aggregated health dashboard.
- [OpenAPI Spec Generation](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/features/openapi): Generate an OpenAPI 3.1 document from your ExpressoTS app with zero annotations, enrich it with real traffic, detect spec drift, and keep clients in sync.

## CLI

- [Overview](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/cli/overview): The ExpressoTS CLI is a single binary that scaffolds projects, generates code, runs your app, and produces production-ready container / CI/CD artifacts.
- [New](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/cli/new): expressots new creates a v4 project from one of the official templates and pre-applies a middleware preset.
- [Running the App](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/cli/running): dev, build, prod, and container-dev: every way the CLI runs your ExpressoTS application.
- [Generate](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/cli/generate): expressots generate scaffolds resources (controllers, use cases, DTOs, interceptors, events, handlers, guards, config files) wired into your DI container.
- [Providers](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/cli/providers): Install, uninstall, and scaffold ExpressoTS providers from the CLI.
- [Scripts](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/cli/scripts): Run any npm script from your package.json via an interactive picker or by name.
- [Studio](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/cli/studio): Launch ExpressoTS Studio from the CLI. Auto-installs @expressots/studio if it isn't already a project devDependency.
- [Info & Resources](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/cli/info): Two read-only commands that print diagnostic information about your environment and a cheat sheet of every CLI command and generate schematic.
- [Containerize & Profile](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/cli/containerize): Generate Dockerfiles, compose files, and Kubernetes manifests. Profile and optimize existing Dockerfiles or built images.
- [CI/CD](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/cli/cicd): Generate CI/CD pipelines for GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI, Jenkins, Bitbucket, and Azure Pipelines.
- [Migrate](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/cli/migrate): Generate migration scaffolds from one deployment platform to another: Heroku to Railway/Render/Fly, Docker Compose to Kubernetes, and more.
- [Costs](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/cli/costs): Estimate and compare cloud deployment costs across AWS, GCP, Azure, Railway, Render, Fly.io, Heroku, and DigitalOcean.
- [Templates](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/cli/templates): Manage the cached CI/CD / Docker / Kubernetes / migration templates.
- [Pricing Data](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/cli/pricing): Sources, cascading fallback, and contributing pricing corrections for the costs command.
- [Contributing](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/cli/contributing): Contribute templates and pricing corrections to the ExpressoTS CLI ecosystem.
- [Template System Architecture](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/cli/architecture): How the CLI fetches, caches, and merges templates from the local cache, remote repository, and embedded fallback.

## STUDIO

- [Overview](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/studio/overview): ExpressoTS Studio is a local developer experience platform for v4 applications. Observability, security, and tooling, all running on your machine.
- [Installation](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/studio/installation): Install and run ExpressoTS Studio against a v4 application.

### Features

- [Status](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/studio/features/status): Studio Status dashboard — uptime, memory, slow routes, error rates, and security grade at a glance.
- [Requests](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/studio/features/requests): Record, inspect, and replay every HTTP call in Studio.
- [Logs](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/studio/features/logs): Stream every framework and app log line in one Studio view.
- [API Client](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/studio/features/api-client): Send HTTP requests from Studio without leaving the UI.
- [Container](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/studio/features/container): Inspect the DI graph binding-by-binding in Studio.
- [Architecture](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/studio/features/architecture): See how controllers, use cases, and providers connect in Studio.
- [Database](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/studio/features/database): Browse your in-memory provider from Studio.
- [Metrics](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/studio/features/metrics): Throughput, per-route latency, slowest endpoints, memory usage, and system health from real traffic in Studio.
- [Replay](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/studio/features/replay): Batch re-run recorded HTTP exchanges and diff responses in Studio.
- [Security](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/studio/features/security): Supply-chain advisories with reachability scoring and OWASP runtime posture in Studio.
- [Coverage](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/studio/features/coverage): Git-aware code coverage, diff coverage, annotated source, and in-Studio test runs.

## GUIDES

- [Example Projects](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/guides/example-projects): Fifteen runnable ExpressoTS v4 examples on GitHub, each mapped to a guide or feature doc.
- [File Upload](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/guides/file-upload): Learn how to handle file uploads in ExpressoTS.
- [Micro API](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/guides/micro-api): Build lightweight, production-ready microservices with ExpressoTS Micro API.
- [Authentication](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/guides/authentication): Wire JWT authentication into an ExpressoTS v4 app using the framework's AuthProvider and guards.
- [Database Integration](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/guides/database-integration): Integrate databases with ExpressoTS v4 using the provider lifecycle and the built-in InMemoryDBProvider.
- [Deployment](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/guides/deployment): Deploy an ExpressoTS app with Docker, Docker Compose, or Kubernetes.
- [Container Development](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/guides/container-development): Develop your ExpressoTS app inside Docker containers with hot reload.
- [Provider Ecosystem](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/guides/provider-ecosystem): Explore ExpressoTS providers for databases, authentication, observability, and more.
- [Building a Provider Package](https://doc.expresso-ts.com/docs/guides/provider-package): Scaffold, build, test, and publish a reusable @expressots/* provider package using the v4 provider template.
